wait.finding: Reviewed at the tagged commit (captured 2026-11-17 from raw.githubusercontent.com at the tagged commit; each body matches its git blob id and size in the tagged tree listing). Native: server/server.go registers every REST route (api/v1/messages, search, message/{id} and its parts, tags, send, info, webui, chaos, swagger) and none blocks until mail arrives, so there is no blocking wait route. Stream candidate, WebSocket GET {webroot}api/events (server/server.go: middleWareFunc(apiWebsocket); apiWebsocket calls websockets.ServeWs and then storage.BroadcastMailboxStats). Producer: internal/storage/messages.go Store commits the insert transaction, sets tags, then calls websockets.Broadcast("new", summary) and BroadcastMailboxStats; frames are JSON {"Type","Data"}. Registration: client.go ServeWs writes the upgrade response first, then sends the client on the hub's unbuffered register channel, and only then starts readPump and writePump; hub.go Run adds it to Clients and increments clientCount in that case. Readiness evidence: the hub sends only to registered clients, so the first hub frame a client receives is ordered after its registration; notifications.go BroadcastMailboxStats sends a "stats" frame 250 ms after it is called, but only one stats broadcast may be pending at a time, so its arrival is not guaranteed. readPump reads with NextReader, so a pong to a client ping comes from the default handler of gorilla/websocket v1.5.3 (go.mod), whose source is not in the tagged tree; readPump starts only after the register send returns, but clientCount is incremented by the hub after that handoff, and Broadcast returns without sending while clientCount reads 0. Loss: Broadcast hands each message to the hub from a new goroutine, so the order of separate broadcasts is not fixed; the hub drops a client whose 256-slot queue is full; writes have a 10 s deadline and pings run every 54 s; nothing is replayed after a gap. Access: middleWareFunc checks the Host header and the CORS origin before the handler; cors.go admits a request with no Origin header, and Basic auth applies only when UI credentials are set.

best_wait.observed: poll: the common 100 ms poll, labelled "no documented wait": native_wait is not_supported (mailpit-server.go), and the api/events WebSocket has no readiness ordered after registration in captured bytes. Its first hub frame is the stats frame, which mailpit-storage-notifications.go does not guarantee (one pending broadcast at most), and a pong comes from gorilla/websocket v1.5.3 (mailpit-go.mod), whose source is not in the tagged tree. Readiness gap, not proof that no channel exists (0132 §7.2.2)

wait.finding: Reviewed the vendored MailHog-Server, goose and gorilla/websocket packages at the tagged commit (captured 2026-11-17 from raw.githubusercontent.com at the tagged commit; each body matches its git blob id and size in the tagged tree listing; the MailHog-Server and goose license files are retained beside them). Native: MailHog-Server api/v1.go and api/v2.go register the message, download, release, search, jim, outgoing-smtp, events and websocket routes; none blocks until mail arrives, so there is no blocking wait route. Producer: smtp/session.go acceptMessage calls storage.Store and then sends the message on the server's message channel before returning; api/api.go forwards each message to the v1 channel and then the v2 channel, each send blocking until its loop takes it. Stream candidate 1, WebSocket GET {WebPath}/api/v2/websocket (api/v2.go): the v2 loop passes each message (the full message JSON) to websockets/hub.go Broadcast, which blocks until the hub loop takes it. Registration: Hub.Serve writes the upgrade response first, then sends the connection on the unbuffered registerChan, which the hub loop adds to its connections in that case, and only then starts writeLoop and readLoop. Readiness evidence: readLoop reads with NextReader; the vendored gorilla/websocket conn.go answers a ping with a pong through its default ping handler, and its read limit (here 1 byte, connection.go) counts only data frames. A pong therefore follows the registration handoff, and the single hub loop takes any later broadcast only after adding the connection. Loss: the hub unregisters a connection whose 256-slot queue is full; writes have a 10 s deadline, pings run every 54 s and a pong is required within 60 s; nothing is replayed after a gap; CheckOrigin admits every origin. Stream candidate 2, server-sent events GET {WebPath}/api/v1/events (api/v1.go, goose.go): AddReceiver writes the 200 text/event-stream header, hijacks the connection and only then registers the receiver; after registration it receives a data event per message and a keepalive event once a minute, and Notify writes to each receiver from a new goroutine. No readiness ordered after registration is shown, so this channel does not qualify.

wait.finding: Reviewed at the tagged commit (captured 2026-11-17 from raw.githubusercontent.com at the tagged commit; each body matches its git blob id and size in the tagged tree listing; the recursive listing of the commit's root tree, asked for with ?recursive=1, binds each nested path to the commit's tree id). Native: Controllers/MessagesController.cs routes api/messages (new, list, {id} and its parts, source, raw, plaintext, html, reply, send, relay, markRead, delete, folders); GetNewSummaries returns summaries newer than a last-seen id at once, and none blocks until mail arrives, so there is no blocking wait route. Stream candidate, ASP.NET Core SignalR: Startup.cs calls AddSignalR, registers NotificationsHub as a singleton, enables UseWebSockets and maps the hub at /hubs/notifications (under BasePath when it is not "/"; the pinned appsettings default is "/"). Producer: Server/Smtp4devServer.cs OnMessageReceived awaits ProcessMessage on the task queue (TaskQueue.cs completes the returned task after the action runs); ProcessMessage adds the message, saves, trims, saves again and then calls NotificationsHub.OnMessagesChanged(mailbox), which sends "messageschanged" with the mailbox name to Clients.All when Clients is set (Hubs/NotificationsHub.cs). Registration and wire protocol are the SignalR framework's (negotiate, handshake, hub-protocol framing), shipped as framework assemblies in the release archive; no source in the tagged tree shows when a connection joins Clients.All relative to the handshake reply. The UI client (ClientApp/src/HubConnectionManager.ts) connects with @microsoft/signalr HubConnectionBuilder. Readiness evidence: NotificationsHub's public methods are hub methods a client may invoke, and each sends to Clients.All, so a client that receives the broadcast of its own invocation (for example OnMailboxesChanged, which sends "mailboxeschanged") was a member of Clients.All at that send. Loss and replay: nothing in the reviewed sources replays a notification after a gap, and OnMessagesChanged sends nothing while the singleton hub's Clients is unset.

wait.finding: Reviewed at the tagged commit (captured 2026-11-17 from raw.githubusercontent.com at the tagged commit; each body matches its git blob id and size in the tagged tree listing; the recursive listing of the commit's root tree, asked for with ?recursive=1, binds each nested path to the commit's tree id). Native: pkg/rest/routes.go registers the mailbox list, show, purge, delete, mark-seen and source routes and the v1/v2 monitor routes; none blocks until mail arrives, so there is no blocking wait route. Stream candidate, WebSocket monitor GET /api/v2/monitor/messages (every mailbox) or /api/v2/monitor/messages/{name} (one mailbox): pkg/server/lifecycle.go mounts the REST routes under /api/ and builds the hub with Web.MonitorHistory (help: INBUCKET_WEB_MONITORHISTORY, default 30; the launch does not set it). The v1 routes send message headers only and drop deletions; v2 sends {"variant":"message-stored"|"message-deleted", ...} events. Producer: pkg/message/manager.go Deliver stores each message (Store.AddMessage) and then emits AfterMessageStored; pkg/extension/async_broker.go runs each listener in a new goroutine; pkg/msghub/hub.go's listener queues a Dispatch operation that records the message in the history ring and relays it to every listener. Registration: pkg/rest/socket_controller.go serveMonitor writes the upgrade response first, then newMsgListener queues hub.AddListener, one hub operation that plays the history ring back to the listener and then registers it, and only after that queue send returns starts the write pump and the read pump. Every hub operation runs in order on one goroutine from one FIFO channel. Readiness evidence: a played-back history event is sent by the AddListener operation itself (only when the ring is non-empty); the read pump reads with ReadMessage, so a pong to a client ping comes from the default handler of gorilla/websocket v1.5.3 (go.mod), whose source is not in the tagged tree; the read pump starts only after AddListener is queued, so any Dispatch queued later runs after the registration. Loss: Receive waits for space in the listener's 100-slot queue or for its close, so a slow listener blocks the hub rather than being dropped; the read limit is 512 bytes; pings run every 54 s and a pong is required within 60 s. Replay: up to MonitorHistory recent messages on registration. The upgrader sets no CheckOrigin, so the library default applies.
